# Revision pairs

Pairs of revisions of one small part (`<case>.old.step.gz`, `<case>.new.step.gz`) for
`tests/revision.rs`. They are quiddity-rust's correspondence fixtures
(`tests/fixtures/revisions`), copied unchanged:

| Case | What changed |
| --- | --- |
| `hole_moved` | the Ø6 hole moved from x = 40 to x = 25 |
| `hole_added` | a Ø7 hole added at (30, 30) |
| `hole_removed` | the Ø7 hole at (30, 30) removed; the holes after it renumber |
| `boss_resized` | the boss Ø20 → Ø26 |
| `plate_thickened` | the plate 10 → 12 thick; its pattern holes are symmetric repeats |
| `whole_part_moved` | the whole part turned and moved, nothing else |

The `complex_*` pairs are made by `complex.py` (build123d; specify-core-rust #56): a 100 × 80 × 10
plate with 4 × Ø6 holes on a Ø60 circle, a pocket, two chamfers and a boss underneath (each
`.old`), changed in ways that read badly before, each `.new`:

| Case | What changed |
| --- | --- |
| `complex_many` | holes 4 × Ø6 → 6 × Ø8, the pocket deeper and wider, a slot added, the chamfers and the boss removed |
| `complex_fillet_all` | R5 fillets on the four corners (the chamfers carry round them) |
| `complex_moved` | the geometry turned 90° and moved, and the holes Ø6 → Ø7 |
| `complex_remodelled` | the same shape, built as two halves |
| `complex_counterbore` | the through holes counterbored |
| `complex_pattern` | 4 holes on Ø60 → 5 on Ø48 |

`gramil_assembly` (under the Open Community License v1: see `LICENSE-gramil`) is two revisions of gramil's assembly (pzfreo/gramil 9171ef6),
12 distinct parts, made by `gramil_assembly.py` from a gramil checkout with its
venv (build123d 0.10.0) and gzipped (`gzip -9`), for `tests/assembly_diff.rs`. Both are the
production build (`process.prototype=False`, as gramil's `scripts/build_production.py`). The
new revision is gramil's defaults; the old has `shaft.drive_plate_mount_depth` 4 (not 5) and
`drive_plate.mount_hole_diameter` 2.2 (not 2.4). So GRM-02 shaft's mount tap goes deeper, GRM-04
drive plate's mount hole goes Ø2.2 → Ø2.4, and the other 10 parts are unchanged. The shaft's end
chamfer is left alone; `gramil_shaft` below isolates that change (#67).

`plate_turned` is a plate and a block, made by `plate_turned.py` with build123d 0.10.0: the new
plate is the old one turned end for end in its own frame and placed as before, for
`tests/assembly_diff.rs` (a part that moved in its own frame is `moved`, not `unchanged`).

`bearing_flange` is build123d's `examples/cast_bearing_unit.py` (Apache-2.0, by Gumyr), an
oval flanged bearing housing with drafted sides, exported with build123d 0.11.0. The new
revision changes two parameters: the flange `A1` 11 → 13 thick and the bolt holes
`Hole(5)` → `Hole(4.5)`, Ø10 → Ø9.

`gramil_shaft` (For #67) is Paul Fremantle's gramil shaft from
[pzfreo/gramil](https://github.com/pzfreo/gramil), commit
`9171ef652e81daf7102c5155531493d36c349b3c`, under the Open Community License v1
(see `LICENSE-gramil`, also covering the generator). `gramil_shaft.py` uses
`gramil.parts.shaft.build_shaft` and gramil's `build123d.export_step` export path.
Both use default `PurflingCutterParams` with `process.prototype=False`; the only
difference is `shaft.end_chamfer`: 0 (old) and 1.5 (new). Reproduce with:

```sh
uv venv --python 3.12 /tmp/gramil-venv
uv pip install --python /tmp/gramil-venv/bin/python /path/to/gramil 'ocp-gordon==0.2.0'
/tmp/gramil-venv/bin/python gramil_shaft.py .
```

Generated with Python 3.12.13, build123d 0.10.0 and cadquery-ocp 7.8.1.1.post1.
Pinning ocp-gordon avoids 0.3.1's incompatible `OCP.collections` import with that
OCP version. The recipe writes both STEPs then gzips them with mtime 0.

The same recipe also writes two negative controls against `gramil_shaft.old`:
`gramil_shaft.shorter` adds the chamfer AND changes `shaft.length` 37.6 → 35.6;
`gramil_shaft.flat_moved` adds the chamfer AND changes `shaft.flat_depth` 0.6 → 0.8.
Their genuine boss height / flat plane changes must remain visible.

`edge_treatment_controls.py` (build123d 0.10.0, run with an output directory) makes
`flat_translated` and `plate_removed`. Both add a 1.5 × 45° top chamfer. The first
moves a finite flat 3 mm along a Ø16 × 40 cylinder, within its unchanged support
plane; three fixed, unequal bores anchor correspondence. The second removes a
10 × 50 × 50 upright from a 100 × 50 × 10 bracket with a Ø16 × 12 boss. The
fixture script gives all positions and dimensions. These guard against treating
plane equality or the presence of a chamfer as sufficient reason to hide a change.

`pmi_split` is a plate with two unequal bores, made by `pmi_split.py`. The new
revision retains the seam of two fused half plates (`SkipClean`): 8 faces become
12 with identical geometry. `tests/revision_pmi.rs` adds foreign flatness controls
on a planar face and its split supports, changing 0.2 to 0.1.

For #87, `named_plate.old/new.step.gz` are generated by `named_plate.py` with
Python 3.12 and `cadquery-ocp-novtk==8.0.1.1.0` (OCCT 8.0). An 80 × 50 plate
with two unequal bores changes thickness 8 → 11 mm. The new shell visits the
same authored primitive faces in reverse order, so indices shift as faces move.
The author assigns cadgen-style names through XCAF sub-shape labels and boolean
history, then enables `write.stepcaf.subshapes.name`. No geometric naming is used.
Reproduce with `python named_plate.py .` from this directory in that venv.

`cadgen_pmi_plate.step.gz` is the geometry exported by xcaf-pmi from its
`tests/fixtures/cadgen_pmi_plate.xbf`, text-to-cad's cadgen 0.8.3 `pmi_plate` at
commit eab58ee8. Its seven authored face names are retained. The source fixture's
MIT redistribution grant and copyright notice are in `LICENSE-cadgen`.
Reproduce from an xcaf-pmi checkout using
`xcaf-pmi tests/fixtures/cadgen_pmi_plate.xbf --step cadgen_pmi_plate.step`,
then gzip with mtime 0. xcaf-pmi uses `cadquery-ocp-novtk>=8.0,<8.1`.


Notes scene regressions (copied without modifying the STEP records; deterministic gzip):
- `xcaf_pmi_plate.step.gz`: editor-team `31-xcaf_pmi_plate.step`, an xcaf-pmi export
  with haecceity 0.2.8 callouts; material-only file block plus two semantic notes.
- `spindle-q137.step.gz`: quiddity-rust `crates/haecceity/tests/fixtures/presentation/`.
- `presentation_plate.step.gz`: quiddity-rust `tests/fixtures/ap242/presentation-placement/plate.step.gz`.
- `cadgen_notes_plate.step.gz`: quiddity-rust `crates/haecceity/tests/fixtures/xcaf/pmi_plate.geom.step.gz`.
The last three mirror #163's geometry checks. The existing NIST CTC-01 fixture completes
the one-block sweep; bare geometry uses accepted defaults to supply notes.

`spindle_pmi.old/new.step.gz` are the editor team's Specify 0.1.7 spindle
revision reproducer (`spindle_pmi_before/after.step.gz`), copied byte for byte.
They cover answered diff scenes retaining stale file semantic ids and a thread
manufacturing note incorrectly paired with a newly numbered location dimension.

`plate_split` is the v0.1.8 git-workflow regression: a 100 × 60 × 10 box with
Ø8 through holes at x = ±30. The new revision cuts a 6 × 60 × 4 box centred
at (0, 0, -5), splitting old bottom face 4 into new faces 4 and 8. These are
the supplied workflow plates, gzipped with mtime 0; `plate_split.py` reproduces
the build123d construction. They check that an orphaned datum cannot become an
accepted default and that saved evidence detects stale face numbering.

`block_face_pushed` (specify-core-rust #180, made with build123d 0.13 / OpenCascade 8.0, Apache-2.0
with this repository) is a 60 × 40 block standing on z = 0, 20 high, its top face then pushed 5 mm
(25 high). Sharp corners and no hole, fillet or other feature, so no feature explains the change:

```python
from build123d import Box, Pos, export_step
def part(height):
    return Pos(0, 0, height / 2) * Box(60, 40, height)
export_step(part(20), "block_face_pushed.old.step"); export_step(part(25), "block_face_pushed.new.step")
```

`plate_side_pushed` (#180, same tools and licence) is a 60 × 60 × 10 plate on the origin with four
Ø6 through holes at (15, 15), (15, 45), (45, 15) and (45, 45), whose +X side face is then pushed
5 mm (65 wide). The holes anchor the match, so an alignment is found (the aligned branch of the
report's `other_faces`):

```python
from build123d import Align, Box, Cylinder, Pos, export_step
MIN = (Align.MIN, Align.MIN, Align.MIN)
def plate(width):
    p = Box(width, 60, 10, align=MIN)
    for x, y in [(15, 15), (15, 45), (45, 15), (45, 45)]:
        p = p - Pos(x, y, 0) * Cylinder(3, 10, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.MIN))
    return p
export_step(plate(60), "plate_side_pushed.old.step"); export_step(plate(65), "plate_side_pushed.new.step")
```

`boss_shortened` (#181, same tools and licence) is made by `top_filleted_boss.py` (build123d
0.11.0, run with an output directory): a 120 × 120 × 10 base with a Ø65 boss whose top edge has
an R3 fillet, shortened from 13 to 8 mm high with the same fillet. Up to quiddity 0.5.2 the
shorter boss dropped its fillet and cap from its height (13 → 5); 0.5.3 measures both (13 → 8).

`symmetric_tie` and `pair_after_removal` (with their `.answers.json`) are the maintainer's
synthetic step-flow scenarios `symmetric` and `remove` (build123d plates, gzipped with no name
or mtime). `symmetric_tie`: a 100 × 60 × 10 plate with Ø6 holes at (30, 30), datum B and H7,
and (70, 30), which moves to (75, 30); the old plate fits the new one turned 180° about Z as
well as it lies. `pair_after_removal`: the Ø8 hole at (80, 15) is removed, so the Ø5 pair's
faces 8, 9 become 7, 8.
